rows.name: Merck & Co.
rows.thesis: A defensive large drugmaker with low volatility (32%), a 4.5% free-cash-flow yield and steady growth; it is ahead of the ETF since purchase.
rows.risks: Only 3.5% above its 200-day average after a 9% weekly drop; the GAAP P/E is distorted by one-off charges.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or a pipeline or patent setback breaks the earnings path.

rows.name: Targa Resources
rows.thesis: Fee-based gas gathering and processing that grows with Permian volumes; the steadiest energy name, ahead of the ETF since purchase.
rows.risks: Net debt is 32% of market value, and lower oil prices could slow Permian drilling.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or management cuts its volume guidance.

rows.name: Nucor
rows.thesis: The leading US steelmaker behind tariff protection: 22% revenue growth, a P/E of 15 and a solid balance sheet; still above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: Cyclical demand risk if the correction becomes a growth scare.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or tariff policy on steel is loosened.

rows.name: CrowdStrike
rows.thesis: The leading cybersecurity platform, with 24% revenue growth and recurring revenue; still 19% above its 200-day average despite the tech selloff.
rows.risks: 80% volatility, and a high valuation going into results confirmed for December 1.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or the December 1 results show annual recurring revenue growth slowing sharply.

rows.name: Hasbro
rows.thesis: Growing (+19% revenue), profitable (18% margin), a 7.8% free-cash-flow yield at a P/E of about 17, and the steadiest share I hold (25% volatility).
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 19% above), or Q4 results show the digital gaming segment slowing sharply.

rows.name: DuPont
rows.thesis: The slimmer post-breakup DuPont is being re-rated: up 7.9% over a month in a falling market, with a 4.1% free-cash-flow yield; it is 22 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
rows.risks: Industrial demand could weaken if the selloff turns into a growth scare.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 4% above), or its lead over the S&P 500 ETF since purchase falls below +5 points.

rows.name: Viatris
rows.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker paying down debt, with a 9.4% free-cash-flow yield; up 6.4% over a month in a falling market, 17 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
rows.risks: High leverage (net debt 51% of market value).
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or debt reduction stalls.

rows.name: Marathon Petroleum
rows.thesis: My only refiner: P/E of 7.2, 21% free-cash-flow yield and heavy buybacks, still 19.5% above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: Refining margins are volatile, and the share is down 20% over a month.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

rows.name: Target Corporation
rows.thesis: Q3 (reported November 18) beat estimates: sales +7.1%, comparable sales +5.6%, traffic +5%, and full-year guidance raised. The share is 2% under its high and rose in a week when the index fell 7.7%, and it fills my zero staples weight at a P/E of 17.
rows.risks: About $0.50 of the Q3 EPS came from one-off tariff refunds, and a 90% 12-month run leaves room for profit-taking.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 20% above), or holiday sales trends reverse the raised guidance.

rows.name: Keysight Technologies
rows.thesis: Record fiscal Q4 on November 19 (revenue $1.99bn, +41%; orders +53%; above the top of guidance) confirms strong AI and networking test demand; the share's drop looks like market selling, not a business problem.
rows.risks: The share is 19% below its 200-day average and no fiscal 2027 guidance was confirmed, so the downtrend could continue.
rows.exit_if: It falls more than 25% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 20 points since purchase, or a fiscal 2027 outlook implies growth below 10%.

rows.name: NetApp
rows.thesis: Data storage tied to AI demand, at a P/E of 22 with a 5.3% free-cash-flow yield and net cash; held into results on December 1.
rows.risks: It is only 0.5% above its 200-day average with hardware peers falling hard.
rows.exit_if: Q2 results or guidance disappoint, or it closes clearly below its 200-day average (more than 3% under).

rows.name: Morgan Stanley
rows.thesis: Wealth-management fees plus a dealmaking recovery: 16% revenue growth, a 25.5% margin and a P/E of 13; my only financials holding against a 13% index weight.
rows.risks: It is 14.8% below its 200-day average, right at my exit line, and dealmaking suffers in selloffs.
rows.exit_if: It falls more than 15% below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 10 points since purchase.

rows.name: Illumina, Inc.
rows.thesis: Q3 beat with raised guidance, a 20% margin and net cash; still 6% above its 200-day average after a sharp pullback.
rows.risks: High volatility (79%) and momentum that has rolled over.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase.

rows.name: Omnicom Group
rows.thesis: Organic growth accelerated to 7.2% in Q3 as the Interpublic merger integration nears completion, with $900 million in targeted synergies. It has a 12% free-cash-flow yield, net cash, trades 4% under its high, and gives the portfolio its first communication-services exposure.
rows.risks: Some of the Q3 lift came from the World Cup and midterm elections, and advertising budgets get cut in a downturn; the GAAP margin is depressed by merger charges.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 8% above), or organic growth falls back below 3%.
